prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands at magic twist angles in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, without a claim on the mechanism of the superconductivity

statement.case_for: I keep B001 alone as my preferred configuration with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, and my preferred configuration has not changed since round 1. The chair's summary confirms that six of eight files place it alone with identical names, and the deciding point for me is the science, not the count. The 2011 continuum model gave a quantitative, falsifiable prediction of flat bands at a specific twist angle. In 2018 an experiment found correlated insulating and superconducting states in exactly that regime, and independent groups have since reproduced them and extended the physics to twisted multilayers and transition-metal dichalcogenides. None of that depends on the pairing mechanism, which is why I think the citation should name the prediction and the observed phases and say nothing about why the material superconducts. A theory-plus-experiment pair of this kind, tested after seven years and confirmed by others for a further eight, is as mature as a field this young can be. The experimental side is thin with one name, but the group leader convention is defensible, and widening it would remove one of the two authors of the decisive prediction.
statement.case_against: The strongest argument against is the one Kroll and Lindroth press, that the content of the discovery is not yet fixed. The mechanism of the superconductivity is open, twist-angle and device variability complicate several of the states, and a committee could reasonably wait. Attribution is also genuinely incomplete. Cao as first author, Fatemi, Dean, Efetov, Young and Yazdani, and the earlier twisted-bilayer band theory that Olsson names all have claims that three names cannot honour, and I cannot fully answer that. B007 is the case I find hardest to rank below B001, because it is mature, cleanly attributed and confirmed in several laboratories. I rank B001 above it because it opened a new class of tunable correlated matter, but I accept that this is a judgement about criteria and not a measurable fact.

responses.point: Kroll treats the unsettled interpretation of the correlated states as the reason B001 should wait, and says B007 is the more defensible configuration on the supplied names, while conceding that B001 has the larger scientific footprint.
responses.response: I take the maturity objection seriously, but I separate two questions. Whether the flat-band correlated and superconducting phases exist and are reproducible is settled by independent groups. Why the superconductivity appears is not, and I would not let that decide the prize if the citation is written so it does not claim an explanation. That is the specific evidence I would ask of someone who ranks B001 lower, namely whether any result under dispute could remove the phases at the predicted angle. I know of none. I agree that B007 is the better fallback and I keep it as my first alternative, but I would not choose it on the grounds that the second has not yet been redefined, since you yourself say that should not carry the argument. The decision between the two is therefore a choice of criterion, and I put field-opening discovery with a tested prediction ahead of an enabling measurement capability this year.

responses.point: Lindroth argues B007 is a sharply defined invention with complete independent confirmation, but names as her main reservation that lattice clocks build on the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize.
responses.response: Your reservation about distinctness is a fair one, and it is partly why I place B007 as an alternative and not above B001. I do not think it is decisive against B007, because magic-wavelength trapping is a separate idea from the comb or from single-ion control, and Katori and Ye are an uncontested pair. Your point that the two-name pair leaves room in the allocation is true in numbers but I do not think it should be a reason to choose it. I also want to correct how you used my earlier remark on B015. I put Cirac and Zoller high for the merits of the proposals, but I agree with you that a theory-only prize is harder to defend than a prediction that was then tested, and that is the same reasoning that favours B001 over B015.

responses.point: Olsson asks whether I would still support B058 if the credit had to be limited to the three names as listed, since Wallraff is outside them.
responses.response: My answer is no. I would not support B058 on the three supplied names, because the experimental demonstration of strong coupling and the later circuit work involved Wallraff, and a citation that omits him would misdescribe the discovery. I also disclosed that B058 is in my own field and I recuse myself from discussion centred on it beyond field-specific information. Together with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which makes a second circuits award this soon hard to justify, I have no reason to pull B058 above B001 and I will not argue for it. I keep it only as a second alternative so that my own opening ranking is on the record. On your own move from B030 to B001, I think you reasoned well in discounting the candidate you know best.

responses.point: Danielsson wants a citation that credits the flat-band prediction and the observed phases and does not claim an explanation of the superconductivity, and argues the theory-experiment split fits three names.
responses.response: We agree on the wording and I have written my citation to say that explicitly. On the experimental credit, you and I both hold that the group leader convention is acceptable. I would add that the committee should be honest about its limits and that the prize rationale, not the three names, should say that other laboratories confirmed the result. I do not accept Mehlig's earlier suggestion of dropping Bistritzer to make room, since the continuum model is a joint Bistritzer-MacDonald paper.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept Jarillo-Herrero as the only experimental name for B001, or whether Cao or another first-author experimentalist should be weighed against a theory name within the three-person limit.
Whether a future result on the superconducting mechanism or on the correlated states could revise the story the citation tells, even though the phases themselves are reproduced.
How much weight the earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure theory should carry in the wording of the theory part, which I cannot resolve from the supplied names.
Whether the committee ends up choosing between B001 and B007 on field-opening novelty or on enabling capability, since I do not think the evidence alone settles that choice.
statement.conflict_note: I direct WACQT and work at Chalmers in superconducting circuits and quantum computing, so B058 (circuit QED) and less directly B015 are in my own field. I have worked with Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson and with Anton Frisk Kockum, and Chalmers hosted researchers connected to the 2025 prize. I also share an institution with Olsson. None of the people credited for B001 or B007 appears in my profile as a collaborator. I would recuse myself from any discussion centred on B058 beyond giving field-specific information, and I identify no other specific conflict.
